subject: Film & Cinema
title: Agnès Varda: The Grandmother of the New Wave
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Agnès Varda: The Grandmother of the New Wave.

hook.text: Varda made her first film in 1955, before any of her male New Wave peers picked up a camera.

buildup.text: Cléo from 5 to 7 followed a woman in real time through Paris, waiting for medical results.

discovery.text: Varda blended documentary and fiction throughout her career, inventing her own form.

twist.text: She was marginalized by critics who centered Godard and Truffaut as the movement's leads.

climax.text: Late in life, Varda received overdue recognition — including an honorary Oscar at 89.

punchline.text: She started the wave but was the last to get credit.

quiz.question: Why is Varda called the 'grandmother' of the French New Wave?
options: She made her first film before the other New Wave directors
